body.statement: Along every sequence \(P_n\in\mathcal P_n\) with \(b_n/a_n\to0\), \(\operatorname{length}(I_n^{\mathrm{out}})/[2\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2)a_n]\to1\) in \(P_n\)-probability, without any prescribed rate at which \(a_n/b_n\) diverges.
body.justification: Every-sequence adaptation rules out a hidden signal pretest that sacrifices slowly diverging regular sequences.
body.gap: Bei--Navjeevan's general result allows a fixed conservativeness allowance away from degeneracy and suggests a tuning-based pretest; the panel literature has no exact all-sequence Gaussian-length constant.
body.consumer: Regular high-loading counterfactual entries retain the same asymptotic length as the established Gaussian interval.
